topic: Sitting on your wallet and other sciatica myths

slides.headline: Is your wallet causing your sciatica?
slides.sub: Sorting the common sciatica myths from what actually tends to help.

slides.title: Myth: it's all your back pocket
slides.body: Sitting on a thick wallet for hours can irritate some people's buttock area. Moving it is an easy change worth trying, but it's rarely the whole story behind leg pain.

slides.title: Myth: sciatica means serious damage
slides.body: Sciatica describes irritated nerve roots sending pain down the leg. It can feel intense, yet most people improve over weeks to a few months with the right mix of movement and time.

slides.title: Myth: rest in bed until it's gone
slides.body: Current guidelines suggest staying as active as you comfortably can. Short walks, changing positions often and gentle movement usually help more than lying still for days.

slides.title: Myth: one adjustment sorts it out
slides.body: Chiropractic care can help some people move more comfortably. It tends to work well as one tool alongside graded exercise, activity advice and a realistic timeline, not as a single quick answer.

slides.title: When to get it checked urgently
slides.body: Numbness around the groin or inner thighs, new bladder or bowel changes, or leg weakness that is getting worse need urgent medical care. Head to your GP or emergency department.

slides.headline: Leg pain that won't let up?
slides.body: Our chiropractors assess your back and leg symptoms, explain what's going on and build a plan that combines hands-on care with exercise.

caption:
Moving your wallet out of your back pocket is a reasonable idea. It's just rarely the full answer to sciatica.

Sciatica describes pain travelling down the leg from irritated nerve roots. It can feel intense, but most people improve over weeks to a few months. Current guidelines suggest staying as active as you comfortably can rather than resting in bed.

Chiropractic care can be one helpful tool, especially combined with graded exercise and a clear plan. Numbness around the groin, bladder or bowel changes, or worsening leg weakness need urgent medical care.

story.headline: Wallet in your back pocket?
story.body: Worth moving, but sciatica is rarely that simple. Staying gently active usually helps more than bed rest.
